# dsh-token-usage
简体中文 | English
A dsh usage plugin that displays model token usage right in the Web UI. The sidebar's **Token Usage*
* entry opens a full-width dashboard — summary cards (with cost), a trend chart, and five detail boa
rds (projects / sessions, models / providers, runtime overhead); the same statistics live in **Setti
ngs → Token Usage** behind five detail tabs (by project / by model / by session / by provider / runt
ime overhead). Both surfaces share date-range and model filters; a single-day range uses an hourly t
rend and wider ranges use daily points.
Repo: <https://github.com/LaoYueHanNi/dsh-token-usage>

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **GitHub direct installs have ended** — the repository no longer carries prebuilt o

utput. Install from npm instead:
>

>
> **Upgrading from a legacy `github:` install (≤ 0.3.7, package name `dsh-token-usage`)?** An in-p
lace `update` fails to load — remove the old name first, then add again. Usage data under `$DSH_HOME
/token-usage/` carries over untouched.
## Features
- **Live recording**: every provider-billed model call is recorded as it happens — tokens, cost, mod
el, session — conversation requests, context-compaction calls, and auxiliary system calls included:
the Auto review authorization reviewer, session-title generation, and reasoning translation. Auxilia
ry calls bill into the totals and the model breakdown. The ones the host proves belong to a session
(session-title generation) also join that session's totals, trend and request pool, tagged with thei
r kind; the rest stay global and are broken out by kind in the **Runtime overhead** board. That hist
ory cannot be backfilled — the host keeps no usage record of those calls, and recording starts with

the first request after upgrading.
- **Web stats page**: filters (date range + model + `1d`/`7d`/`30
d` shortcuts), eight compact summary cards in two rows, and a trend chart (hourly for one day, daily
for wider ranges; hover a point for its total). The request card carries **failed** and **overhead*
* pills. The detail block is a five-tab switcher — **projects / models / sessions / providers / runt
ime overhead** — sharing the dashboard's row layout: project rows aggregate every matching root sess
ion before the session list is capped; directory-tail grouping intentionally merges folders with the
same final segment. Rows sort by total tokens or cost (sessions also by last activity), and **Ctrl+
click** on a listed session row opens that conversation (the host restores its last-selected view ta
b). The runtime-overhead tab breaks auxiliary calls down by kind; the by-provider tab lists each pro
vider's usage by its route key — see the next entry, **Provider usage dimension**.
[该节后续省略]
## Model pricing
Costs are billed per record at its own timestamp. Identification or pricing-rule changes reselect hi
storical rates from raw records on the next read. Models resolve through full original ID matching,
provider-prefix ID matching, then upstream aliasPatterns (deprecated aliases are ignored), all ignor
ing case while preserving versions and model variants. Unknown or ambiguous names have no inferred p
rice. The single source is a cloud mirror auto-synced on every startup — pricing corrections belong
upstream in the model-price-table feed, so every user benefits at once. A hand-edited `pricing.json`
is no longer read; if you maintain one it is silently ignored after upgrading (the file is left on
disk). Upgrading from 0.4.1 or earlier to 0.4.2 triggers a one-time full rebuild of the usage rollup
the first time the stats page is read — the larger the history, the longer it takes; this is expect
ed. An invalid new feed keeps the previous valid mirror. If pricing is unavailable or history cannot
be fully repriced, available usage remains visible while unreliable costs are hidden with a reason.
Missing entries in a valid feed are warned separately. Unpriced names offer local search, full rule
g entries in a valid feed are warned separately. Unpriced names offer local search, full rule [长行截断]
## Configuration
### Data directory
Editable on this plugin's **configuration card** in the host's **Plugins** page: saving an absolute
path takes effect immediately — history migrates automatically, no restart, no manual move. Blank ke
eps the default `~/.dsh/token-usage/`. A save is refused while a conversation is in progress; wait f
or it to end, then save again. Or set it directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Pricing region
The pricing mirror follows your region: **Gitee** by default (fast inside mainland China) or the **G
itHub mirror** of the same table — pick once on the **Pricing region** dropdown of that configuratio
n card in the host's Plugins page, or via config. The pick also drives the display currency (¥ RMB v
s $ USD at the table's exchange rate).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Provider quota
The input-bar button follows the currently selected provider and opens a panel with remaining quota
(API-key providers share the inference key; the DeepSeek account reads the signed-in balance):
| Provider | Shows |

| Zhipu GLM Coding Plan (CN / international) | 5-hour, weekly (some plans also monthly) |
| Kimi For

Coding | 5-hour, monthly (legacy responses: weekly) |
| MiniMax Coding Plan (CN / international) |

5-hour, weekly |
| OpenCode Go | 5-hour, weekly, monthly |
| Command Code | 5-hour, weekly, monthly

|
| DeepSeek (official API key) | ¥ account balance |
| DeepSeek account | topped-up balance, grante

d balance |
| OpenRouter | $ remaining credits |
| Magpie gateway | every upstream account's quota c
ards, scoped to the selected model's provider (routing groups show the whole fleet) |
Unsupported providers hide the button; a failed query can be retried from the panel. On by default;
turn it off with `quota.enabled: false`. Not supported yet: Volcengine, ZenMux, Zhipu Team plan, Cla
ude / Codex / Gemini / Grok official subscriptions, GitHub Copilot.
A magpie route needs no setup: declare any OpenAI-compatible provider whose base URL points at the g
ateway (`http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1` by default) — the plugin probes the gateway's hello and reads its
aggregated quota report. The gateway key goes in the provider's API key when the gateway is shared
from another machine; a loopback gateway needs none.
